beats.text: Astronomers in Prague voted on what a planet is.
beats.note: The International Astronomical Union passed a definition at its General Assembly. Pluto was the casualty.

beats.text: A planet must pass three tests.
beats.note: It orbits the Sun, it is nearly round, and it has cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit.

beats.text: The first draft would have added planets.
beats.note: A proposal published on 16 August would have made Ceres, Charon and Eris planets, with twelve more candidates.

beats.text: Open meetings killed it within a week.
beats.note: Members heavily defeated the Pluto-like object proposals on 22 August, and a new draft replaced it.

beats.context: In favour of naming Pluto a dwarf planet, against 157.

beats.text: Pluto became the prototype of a new category.
beats.note: Resolution 6A called it a dwarf planet and the prototype of trans-Neptunian objects.

beats.text: Pluto did not change. The definition did.

beats.line: A label is a decision, not a discovery.
